agree.reason: The offer to share invoices and the 20-mile chain gap answer both of her doubts with things she can check, so a skeptical director may well take the meeting, though nothing shows her what the losses add up to.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported claim that a third will close, refuses to tie the nine closures to rates, and adds no facts; calling 22% "one in five" understates a little.

works_the_facts.reason: Every figure is quoted raw: it never multiplies $1.80 by Reilly Drug's 3,100 prescriptions to show about $5,580 a year lost at one store, and it turns 22% into a smaller-sounding "one in five."

right_comparison.reason: It describes the alternative accurately (a drive of more than 20 miles to a chain, or mail order, in 14 counties) and adds the two pharmacies that say they will stop filling, though it gives no trend beyond the nine closures.

qualification.reason: The hedge on the closures is honest, and the ask is tied to checkable dates (May 1 meeting, July 1 renewal) and a stated consequence (two pharmacies stop filling), though the consequence has no date attached.

objections.reason: Her "they complain every year" view is met by the offer to open the invoices, and her "plenty of chains" view by the 14 counties where the nearest chain is more than 20 miles away; it raises no objection the facts already answer.

fit.reason: It is a signed open letter of about one page, suited both to the plan and to newspaper readers.
